data.one_liner: Integrates Twilio's Programmable Voice SDK to add VoIP calling into Flutter applications.
data.what_it_does: Provides an interface to Twilio's Programmable Voice SDK, enabling apps to receive and place voice-over-IP (VoIP) calls across Android, iOS, Web, and macOS. It handles native call screens, CallKit integration, and call quality metrics.
use_when: You need to add VoIP calling powered by Twilio into a Flutter app.
Your application requires native call incoming/outgoing user interfaces on iOS and Android.
avoid_when: You are building a general-purpose audio/video streaming app that does not use Twilio.
You want a pure Dart audio recording or playback library without VoIP networking.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, macOS, and Web.
Integrates with platform-native VoIP features like CallKit on iOS and ConnectionService on Android.
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific setup and configuration for push notifications and permissions.
Android and macOS carry specific configuration limitations and known setup complexities.
data.setup_notes: Requires native configuration for FCM on Android, CallKit assets on iOS, and appropriate permission declarations such as microphone, phone state, and phone numbers.
